paper_b.title: Broken Replica Symmetry Bounds in the Mean Field Spin Glass Model (Guerra, 2002)

metadata.description: Guerra and Talagrand provide complementary halves of the proof of the Parisi formula for the SK spin glass. Guerra (2002) proves the lower bound (free energy >= Parisi expression) via an elegant interpolation argument. Talagrand (2006) proves the matching upper bound (free energy <= Parisi expression) via the cavity method and ultrametricity. Together they establish the Parisi formula exactly. These are alternative proofs of the two complementary inequalities, not alternative proofs of the same statement.

matches.explanation: Both define the identical SK model with Gaussian couplings and study the same quantity: the quenched free energy per site $p_N = \frac{1}{N} \mathbb{E} \log Z_N$. Same Hamiltonian, same limit.

Both define the Parisi functional (with its RSB order parameter) as the conjectured value of the free energy. The mathematical object is identical: a variational expression over non-decreasing functions on $[0,1]$, involving the Parisi PDE/recursion.

The two theorems are complementary halves of the same equality. Guerra: $p_N \geq \mathcal{P}(\mu)$ (lower bound on free energy). Talagrand: $\lim p_N \leq \inf_\mu \mathcal{P}(\mu)$ (upper bound). Together: $\lim p_N = \inf_\mu \mathcal{P}(\mu)$. Opposite inequality directions, same target.

Completely different proof techniques. Guerra: simple interpolation between SK model and Parisi reference system, showing monotonicity of the interpolating pressure. Talagrand: cavity method (adding one spin at a time) + Ghirlanda-Guerra identities + ultrametricity + Ruelle probability cascades. Guerra's proof is 5 pages; Talagrand's is 60+.
Guerra's interpolation method (introducing parameter $t$ connecting SK to a solvable reference system) is specific to the lower bound proof. Talagrand uses entirely different techniques.
Guerra's sum rule expressing the difference as a non-negative integral is specific to the interpolation approach.

Both papers remark on the elegance of their respective approaches. Guerra emphasizes the simplicity of interpolation vs. the replica trick. Talagrand acknowledges Guerra's contribution and notes the asymmetry in difficulty between the two bounds.

Both reference the joint resolution of the Parisi conjecture. Guerra notes his bound is complementary to an expected matching upper bound; Talagrand provides that upper bound and notes the combined result resolves the 25-year conjecture.
